title: Finite flat modules over integral restricted-series rings are finitely presented
statement: Let $K$ be a complete field with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $V=\{a\in K:|a|\le1\}$ be its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring]. For an integer $r\ge0$ put $S=V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$, the ring of formal power series with coefficients tending to zero [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Let $Q$ be a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with its $V$-module structure given by constant series. If $Q$ is flat over $V$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $Q$ is finitely presented as an $S$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Section 2.3, Theorem 4, printed p. 130 (PDF page 131), height-one case; primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Define $w:S^s\twoheadrightarrow Q$ by $w(a_1,\ldots,a_s)=\sum_j a_jq_j$, and put $N=\ker w$. This gives the exact sequence $0\to N\to S^s\xrightarrow{w}Q\to0$. The empty generating family is allowed when $Q=0$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Theorem 4, height-one proof, printed p. 130; online primary PDF. Uses Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22.

proof.text: For $0\ne a\in V$, multiplication by $a$ on $V$ is injective, since $V\subset K$. Flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] makes its tensor product with $Q$ injective. Under $V\otimes_V Q\to Q$, $b\otimes q\mapsto bq$, with inverse $q\mapsto1\otimes q$, this map is multiplication by $a$ on $Q$. Thus $aq=0$ implies $q=0$. In particular, if $x\in S^s$ and $ax\in N$, then $aw(x)=0$, hence $w(x)=0$ and $x\in N$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Theorem 4, height-one proof, printed p. 130; online primary PDF. Uses Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22.

proof.text: Let $D=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ and let $L\subseteq D^s$ be the $D$-span of $N$, using coefficientwise inclusions $S\subset D$ [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. We prove $L\cap S^s=N$. Choose $\pi\in K$ with $0<|\pi|<1$; such an element exists by nontriviality, taking an inverse if necessary. If $x=\sum_{i=1}^k d_in_i\in L\cap S^s$ with $d_i\in D$ and $n_i\in N$, the coefficient norms of these finitely many $d_i$ have a common finite bound $B$: outside finite sets they are less than $1$, since they tend to zero. Choose $m\ge0$ with $|\pi|^m B\le1$. Then $\pi^m d_i\in S$, since its coefficients lie in $V$ and still tend to zero. Consequently $\pi^m x\in N$, and Step 2 gives $x\in N$. The reverse inclusion follows from the definition of $L$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Theorem 4, height-one proof, printed p. 130; online primary PDF. Uses Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tate-submodule-norm-controlled-generators] to the $D$-submodule $L\subseteq D^s$ from Step 3. It gives finitely many $v_i\in L$ of norm $1$ and representations $x=\sum_i f_iv_i$ with $\|f_i\|_G\le\|x\|$. Norm at most $1$ means precisely that every coefficient belongs to $V$, so each $v_i$ lies in $S^s$, and hence in $N$ by Step 3. For $x\in N\subseteq S^s$ one has $\|x\|\le1$, so the representing $f_i$ belong to $S$. Thus $N=\sum_i Sv_i$.

source.place: Section 2.3, Theorem 4, height-one proof, printed p. 130; online primary PDF. Uses Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22.

proof.text: Let $h$ be the number of vectors from Step 4. The map $S^h\to S^s$ sending the $i$th standard vector to $v_i$ has image exactly $N=\ker w$. Therefore $S^h\to S^s\xrightarrow{w}Q\to0$ is exact, which is a finite presentation [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Section 2.3, Theorem 4, height-one proof, printed p. 130; online primary PDF. Uses Section 1.3, Corollary 10, printed pp. 21–22.

The new node is a faithful copy of 1.3/10 (printed pp.21–22): any T_n-submodule of T_n^s has generators of norm 1 with |f_i|≤|x|. The chapter-1 standing hypotheses (K complete, absolute value nontrivial) match it. Its proof needs no discreteness. The node is statement-only and self-contained. I tested L=0, s=0, L=D^s and r=0. It does not duplicate any DAG node: tate-ideal-best-approximation is BGR strict closedness without generators, and saturated-submodule-finite, quotient-complete and submodule-adic-topology are downstream. It creates no cycle and is not a clause of the item. The item's steps follow the height-one proof of 2.3/4 (printed p.130). Step 1 takes generators and N=ker w. Step 2 gets torsion-freeness from the tensor-injectivity definition of flatness, so N is saturated. Step 3 proves L∩S^s=N using a common coefficient bound and a power of π; this is Bosch's N⊗K∩R⟨ζ⟩^s=N. Step 4: the norm-1 v_i lie in N, and the norm bound puts the f_i in S. Step 5 matches the exact-sequence definition. Edge cases checked: Q=0, Q free, and S/(π) correctly excluded; non-discrete V is allowed. The statement is unchanged and there are no tool_uses or SGA citations. No fixes.
